        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.T = int(spec.n_types)
        self.P = int(spec.n_place)
        self.L = len(LAYOUTS)
        self.shifts = sorted(set([lay[4] for lay in LAYOUTS]))
        cin = spec.in_channels + self.L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.hmix = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.hout = nn.Conv2d(HID, self.L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.hout.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.hout.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, len(self.shifts))
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        cm, tr, fy, fx = lay[0], lay[1], lay[2], lay[3]
        b = m.shape[0]
        if cm:
            if tr:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.X, self.Y, self.T).permute(0, 3, 2, 1)
            else:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.Y, self.X, self.T).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
        else:
            if tr:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.X, self.Y).transpose(2, 3)
            else:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        return g

    def from_grid(self, g, lay):
        cm, tr, fy, fx = lay[0], lay[1], lay[2], lay[3]
        b = g.shape[0]
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        if cm:
            if tr:
                g = g.permute(0, 3, 2, 1)
            else:
                g = g.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)
        else:
            if tr:
                g = g.transpose(2, 3)
        return g.reshape(b, -1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        b = obs.shape[0]
        P = self.P
        mf = mask.to(obs.dtype)
        grids = [self.to_grid(mf[:, lay[4]:lay[4] + P], lay) for lay in LAYOUTS]
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, self.Y, 1).expand(b, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, self.X).expand(b, 1, self.Y, self.X)

        f = F.relu(h + self.c2(h))
        o = self.hout(F.relu(self.hmix(f)))
        logits = None
        for i, lay in enumerate(LAYOUTS):
            part = self.from_grid(o[:, i * self.T:(i + 1) * self.T], lay)
            sh = lay[4]
            part = F.pad(part, (sh, 1 - sh))
            logits = part if logits is None else logits + part
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        d = self.done_head(g)
        for j, sh in enumerate(self.shifts):
            idx = P if sh == 0 else 0
            logits = logits + F.pad(d[:, j:j + 1], (idx, P - idx))
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

    return Net(spec)

        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, len(self.shifts))
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def to_grid(self, m, lay):
        cm, tr, fy, fx = lay[0], lay[1], lay[2], lay[3]
        b = m.shape[0]

            if tr:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.X, self.Y, self.T).permute(0, 3, 2, 1)
            else:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.Y, self.X, self.T).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)

            if tr:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.X, self.Y).transpose(2, 3)
            else:
                g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        return g

        cm, tr, fy, fx = lay[0], lay[1], lay[2], lay[3]

        if fx:

        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 48
PROJ = 16
HID = 16
LAYOUTS = [(False, False, False), (True, False, False), (False, True, False), (False, False, True)]


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.T = int(spec.n_types)
        self.P = int(spec.n_place)
        self.L = len(LAYOUTS)
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        cin = spec.in_channels + self.L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * PROJ, HID, 1) for _ in range(self.L * self.T)])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in range(self.L * self.T)])
        for o in self.outs:
            nn.init.normal_(o.weight, std=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(o.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def to_grid(self, m, tr, fy, fx):
        b = m.shape[0]
        if tr:
            g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.X, self.Y).transpose(2, 3)
        else:
            g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        return g

    def from_grid(self, g, tr, fy, fx):
        b = g.shape[0]
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        if tr:
            g = g.transpose(2, 3)
        return g.reshape(b, -1)

    def pool_feats(self, p, wy, wx, fy, fx):
        if wy * wx == 1:
            return torch.cat([p, p, p], dim=1)
        pt = wy - 1 if fy else 0
        pb = 0 if fy else wy - 1
        pl = wx - 1 if fx else 0
        pr = 0 if fx else wx - 1
        q = F.pad(p, (pl, pr, pt, pb))
        mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (wy, wx), stride=1)
        mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (wy, wx), stride=1)
        av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (wy, wx), stride=1)
        return torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        b = obs.shape[0]
        m = mask[:, :self.P].to(obs.dtype)
        grids = [self.to_grid(m, lay[0], lay[1], lay[2]) for lay in LAYOUTS]
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, self.Y, 1).expand(b, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, self.X).expand(b, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        x = torch.cat([obs] + grids + [ys, xs], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(x)
        h = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(h + self.c2(h))
        p = F.relu(self.proj(f))
        place = None
        k = 0
        for lay in LAYOUTS:
            tr, fy, fx = lay[0], lay[1], lay[2]
            maps = []
            for t in range(self.T):
                dy, dx = self.fps[t]
                if tr:
                    wy, wx = dx, dy
                else:
                    wy, wx = dy, dx
                z = self.pool_feats(p, wy, wx, fy, fx)
                hh = F.relu(self.mix[k](z))
                maps.append(self.outs[k](hh))
                k += 1
            o = torch.cat(maps, dim=1)
            part = self.from_grid(o, tr, fy, fx)
            place = part if place is None else place + part
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        d = self.done_head(g)
        for j, sh in enumerate(self.shifts):
            idx = P if sh == 0 else 0
            logits = logits + F.pad(d[:, j:j + 1], (idx, P - idx))
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: One main change to mask4: the mean and max pooled over the grid pass through a learned projection and are added to every cell's head features before the per-type output maps. The 1x1 head sees only a 5x5 neighbourhood, so it cannot judge order, such as whether a brick would seal off target cells elsewhere or whether a cell should wait. Global context can supply that. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 48
HID = 32
LAYOUTS = [(False, False, False), (True, False, False), (False, True, False), (False, False, True)]


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.X = int(spec.X)
        self.Y = int(spec.Y)
        self.T = int(spec.n_types)
        self.P = int(spec.n_place)
        self.L = len(LAYOUTS)
        cin = spec.in_channels + self.L * self.T + 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(cin, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.gproj = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, HID)
        self.hmix = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.hout = nn.Conv2d(HID, self.L * self.T, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.hout.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.hout.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def to_grid(self, m, tr, fy, fx):
        b = m.shape[0]
        if tr:
            g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.X, self.Y).transpose(2, 3)
        else:
            g = m.reshape(b, self.T, self.Y, self.X)
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        return g

    def from_grid(self, g, tr, fy, fx):
        b = g.shape[0]
        dims = []
        if fy:
            dims.append(2)
        if fx:
            dims.append(3)
        if len(dims) > 0:
            g = g.flip(dims)
        if tr:
            g = g.transpose(2, 3)
        return g.reshape(b, -1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        b = obs.shape[0]
        m = mask[:, :self.P].to(obs.dtype)
        grids = [self.to_grid(m, lay[0], lay[1], lay[2]) for lay in LAYOUTS]
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, self.Y, 1).expand(b, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, self.X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, self.X).expand(b, 1, self.Y, self.X)
        x = torch.cat([obs] + grids + [ys, xs], dim=1)
        s = self.stem(x)
        h = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(h + self.c2(h))
        gv = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gc = self.gproj(gv).unsqueeze(2).unsqueeze(3)
        o = self.hout(F.relu(self.hmix(f) + gc))
        place = None
        for i, lay in enumerate(LAYOUTS):
            part = self.from_grid(o[:, i * self.T:(i + 1) * self.T], lay[0], lay[1], lay[2])
            place = part if place is None else place + part
        g = self.glob(gv)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: No trials have run in this search yet. Across 84 earlier trials, only one network scored above 0. It feeds the legal-action mask in as channels under several layouts and builds placement logits from per-type output maps laid out the same ways. Changing only the training recipe always scored 0. That suggests the action layout in some worlds differs from what the description says, and the mask lets the network find and match the real layout. So this round first reproduces that design under the default recipe as a baseline for this world. The second candidate tests all 8 flip-and-transpose layouts, in case this world differs in a way the original 4 do not cover. The third keeps the 4-layout network and sets ppo_epochs to 2, which about doubles the training steps (about 243k instead of 131k). Each network costs about the same compute per sample as the starting one (about 1x). Seeds that score exactly 0 point to a mismatch with the world rather than bad luck.
analyses.2: Every trial scored 0, including the mask-layout family that worked in one earlier world. Using all 8 rotations and flips (mask8) also scored 0, and so did 2 PPO epochs. Late training success was at or near 0 in every run (0.0003 at most), so no seed learned. This world's deviation is probably not a spatial rotation or flip between the observation grid and the action index. Changes to the recipe are unlikely to help, because past evidence says recipe-only changes never gave a signal. Two simple index deviations remain untested. In the first, the action index is cell-major (a = cell*T + t) instead of type-major. In the second, DONE sits at index 0, which shifts every placement index by one. These are cheap to hedge in the same layout family. Each one appears in one candidate on its own, and a third candidate combines them so a positive result can be traced back.
analyses.3: All six trials scored 0 on both seeds. Late training success was at most 0.0006, so none of them learned at all. The mask-layout family has now hedged against every reading order of the action index we can name: 4 and 8 dihedral layouts, cell-major order, and DONE placed first. None of it helped, so this world's deviation is probably not in action indexing. Two other explanations are left. First, the observation may not line up with the actions or with itself. Its memory layout could be channel-last, which would scramble it before any convolution sees it. Or the target channels could be mirrored relative to the build channels, which a convolution cannot undo. Second, the policy head may lack footprint structure: the mask4 net dropped the starting net's footprint pooling. This round tests both obs-view hedges cheaply (each costs about 1.1–1.25x the starting compute) and refines mask4 with footprint-window pooling that matches each layout.
analyses.4: Nine trials, all at 0 dev success, with late training success at most 0.0006. The mask4 family, the only design that has scored in any world, did not carry over here. Each hedge tried on its own also failed. Those hedges were: dihedral mask layouts; cell-major and DONE-first index orders; reshaped and dihedral views of the observation; footprint pooling; and a recipe with more samples. A single deviation of one of these kinds now looks unlikely. Two remaining explanations seem plausible. First, two deviations may act together, for example a different index order plus a re-laid observation, which no single hedge covers. Second, the net may lack the global context it needs to choose placement order, or the credit assignment may be too weak for this world's reward. With 3 trials left I will test three things: one combined hedge, one net that adds global context to each cell's output, and that same net with a recipe for longer horizons.
